name: TOGAF 9 Foundation (Part 1)
description: Enterprise architecture fundamentals: the ADM, deliverables, the Enterprise Continuum, and core concepts.

questions.text: In TOGAF, what does ADM stand for?
questions.explanation: The Architecture Development Method (ADM) is the core of TOGAF — a step-by-step, iterative approach to developing and managing an enterprise architecture.

questions.text: Which ADM phase establishes the architecture project, obtains approvals, and defines the scope and constraints?
questions.explanation: Phase A: Architecture Vision initiates an ADM cycle — it defines scope, identifies stakeholders, creates the Architecture Vision, and obtains approval to proceed.

questions.text: What are the four architecture domains addressed by TOGAF?
questions.explanation: TOGAF addresses Business, Data, Application, and Technology architectures. Data and Application are often grouped together as the Information Systems Architectures.

questions.text: Which TOGAF concept is a classification system used to organize architecture artifacts in the Architecture Repository?
questions.explanation: The Enterprise Continuum provides a framework and classification for categorizing architecture and solution artifacts, ranging from generic Foundation Architectures to Organization-Specific Architectures.

questions.text: What document is the deliverable that defines the scope and approach to complete an architecture project, and is signed off by sponsors?
questions.explanation: The Statement of Architecture Work defines the scope, approach, schedule, and resources for an architecture engagement and is approved by the sponsoring stakeholders.

questions.text: Which TWO of the following are phases of the TOGAF ADM?
questions.explanation: Phase B: Business Architecture and Phase E: Opportunities and Solutions are ADM phases. 'Architecture Marketing' and 'Vendor Selection' are not ADM phases.

questions.text: What is the central repository of all architecture assets, including governance logs and reference models, called in TOGAF?
questions.explanation: The Architecture Repository stores architecture artifacts and deliverables: the Architecture Metamodel, Landscape, Standards Information Base, Reference Library, and Governance Log.

questions.text: Which ADM phase is at the center of the ADM cycle and operates throughout all phases?
questions.explanation: Requirements Management sits at the center of the ADM graphic; it is a continuous process that manages architecture requirements across every phase, though it does not itself dictate priorities.
